title: The 1959 England tour
summary: They leave in December 1958 and reach Liverpool and London, meeting Ken Collier's brass band at the station; Sweden and Denmark follow.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I think it was Cavalier. Yeah, I'm more than sure it was Cavalier. Because we had Tom Jefferson on trumpet at that time. Well, anyway, after we got through playing in Frisco, where we came on back home, where Elton, he stopped off in Los Angeles, so he was going to make up his mind to stay there. Well, sure enough, he did. So we came on back home, and we started to play a little odd jobs around town, you know, until something else was popped. So sure enough, came the word from England that they wanted to ban over there. Well, we went over there. We left on the 28th of December, 1958. And we arrived in London, in Liverpool, in early January of 1959. I think it was around the 6th or the 7th or something like that. But anyway, we got there before the 10th of January. Well, we stayed overnight in Liverpool, then we went on up to London. Got trained. We got to London. Ken Collier had his brass band out at the station, the Union Station. They had one over there, you know. And they was playing so much like New Orleans. I said, now I wanted Poison and them to beat us over here and got the band lined up, because I couldn't see for the crowd, you know. Well, as we was marching up to the front, I found out it was Ken Collier's brass band. And they was playing just a little while to stay here. I said, that sounds so much like Poison's brass band. And it was them. Well, Barry, he was on drums. Well, I hadn't met none of them fellas yet, but I hadn't met Ken Collier when he toured over here with us. So we went on to a hotel. I was so nervous. When we got to the hotel, they saw I was shaking. So Jimmy Ashman said, you want a hot cup of tea? He said, quads your nerves. I said, I'd have to have something. Because they wasn't serving the guy that out. So I said, I got to have something, Jimmy. I said, so he gave me a hot cup of tea. And I got all right. Well, we stopped at that hotel, the Empirical Hotel. Well, we stopped there for a little time. Well, in fact, it was a whole week before we did go to work. It gave us a lot of time to get around and view the sights and meet a lot of the people and everything, you know. So, we played, we came back, the first job was to play in Liverpool. And after we left Liverpool, then we started going to Manchester, Birmingham, Brighton, and all them different places playing concerts. Well, we played there, I think, around there for about a month. After we left there, we went to Sweden. No, Denmark. Went to Denmark. We played a concert there. We stayed there for about a week. We left from there. We went to Sweden. What do you call it? Stockholm, Sweden. We played a concert over there in a big gymnasium. And they had a wonderful crowd that turned out. And we was greeted wonderfully by the people. Before we had a chance to start playing, we was on a march to the place. And they wanted to know if we was coming back. I said, yeah, we'll be back. You know, make them feel good. Well, it snowed so much in Sweden, we didn't have a chance to get out to see anything. I mean, it snowed all. When we got there, it snowed and we left, it was snowing. So, I had boys that wanted something to drink. I said, well, I'll go get it. I said, how close is the place? I said, right around the corner. So, when I walked outside, man, ice looked like it was about that thick on the sidewalk. So, I kind of skidded around the corner and got us a bottle. And we all stayed up in the hotel and had two newspaper girl reporters came by and wanted to interview us. And so, we all sat down and drank. So, they forgot the interviews. So, they went on home, you see. And then, we came back to Sweden. Well, anyway, we came back to Denmark.
Yeah, that's Sweden. Yeah, that's right. That was in Sweden.
Yeah, then you went back to Denmark.
